51546124.protein: Myeloid differentiation primary response protein MyD88
51546124.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to human MyD88 TIR domain assessed as equilibrium dissociation constant by SPR analysis

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Surface Plasmon Resonance Assay. The binding affinity of c17 or M2-17 to the human MyD88 TIR domain was investigated by SPR assay utilizing a Biacore T200 equipped with CM5 sensor chips (GE Healthcare) at 22 °C. After activation with 40 mM EDC and 10 mM sNHS in water, MyD88 protein (in acetate acid buffer, pH 5.5) was immobilized on the sensor. c17 or M2-17 samples were prepared with running buffer at the given concentrations (PBS, 0.1% SDS, 5% DMSO, and 0.05% Tween-20). The samples were injected concurrently at five different concentrations. Biacore 4000 and Biacore T200 evaluation software (GE Healthcare) was used for data collection and analysis.
original_paragraph.Figure 2 caption: Figure 2. Hit compound identification. (A) Virtual screen workflow. (B) SPR analysis of M2-17 in different concentrations to bind to the MyD88 protein. (C) ELISA result of M2-17 on the release of IL-6 induced by 0.5 μg/mL LPS. Each bar represents the mean ± standard error of the mean (SEM) in three independent experiments. *p < 0.05, **p < 0.01 vs the LPS-only group.
original_paragraph.Figure 4 caption: Figure 4. (A) IL-6 levels were measured by ELISA assay. (B) TNF-α levels were measured by ELISA assay. (C) SPR analysis of c17 in different concentrations to bind to MyD88. (D) Co-IP results indicating the effect of c17 pretreatment on TLR4-MyD88 interaction in J774A.1 cell exposed to LPS.
original_paragraph.Results and Discussion: Moreover, an ELISA assay was used to demonstrate the M2-17’s anti-inflammatory effect on the release of cytokines induced by the LPS challenge, as MyD88 plays a crucial role in the TLR/IL-1R pathway in the control of the innate immune response. Figure 2C demonstrates that M2-17 significantly suppressed the IL-6 production by J774A.1 macrophages. After selecting compounds, they were put through a Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) assay to determine how well they bound to the MyD88 protein. M2-17, out of all of the compounds examined, showed the best binding affinity to MyD88 (Kd = 7.95 × 10⁻⁴ M) (Figure 2B).
original_paragraph.Conclusions: The activity of a4 and c17 was investigated using SPR and co-IP assay. The active compound c17, with a magnitude lower Kd value than M2-17, was found to bind directly to MyD88 and interfere with the interaction between MyD88 and TLR4. In addition, c17 downregulated the NF-κB pathway by restoring the IkB-α and reducing the translocation of p65 into the nucleus. Moreover, c17 treatment led to c17 accumulation in rat lungs and suppressed LPS-induced ALI in a mouse model. Furthermore, c17 displayed low toxicity in vivo. Based on these results, c17 could be employed as a lead structure in the development of MyD88 inhibitors and as a potential therapeutic strategy for the treatment of ALI.

analyte.concentration_range: 5.94×10⁻⁶ M to 4.75×10⁻⁵ M (as shown in Figure 4C for c17; M2-17 tested at five different concentrations)

data_analysis.software: Biacore 4000 and Biacore T200 evaluation software (GE Healthcare)
